failures.triage_note: Fix A (the /balance URL bug) IS fixed: src/blocks/user-dashboard/view.js's refreshCreditsBalanceAfterCheckout -> tryFetch() now correctly requests /wp-json/wbcom-credits/v1/wb-listora/balance (confirmed in both src/ and the rebuilt build/blocks/user-dashboard/view.js bundle, build newer than source). But the fetch call sends NO 'X-WP-Nonce' header, and neither does the sibling claimOnce() call three lines above it — both reference `window.listoraDashboard.restNonce`, a global that is never localized anywhere in the codebase (grepped blocks/user-dashboard + includes, zero hits for wp_localize_script/wp_add_inline_script producing `listoraDashboard`). WordPress core's rest_cookie_check_errors() responds to a cookie-authenticated request with a missing X-WP-Nonce header by calling wp_set_current_user(0) and treating it as fully anonymous, so the SDK's check_balance_permission() correctly rejects it with 401 rest_forbidden ('Sorry, you are not allowed to do that.'). Reproduced live end-to-end: navigated to /my-listings/?wbcom_credits=success&credits=100&gateway=stripe#credits as credituser, watched the network tab — every one of the ~10 polls over 30s returned 401, and the banner fell through to 'Your credits will appear shortly — refresh in a moment if not.' exactly as before the fix, just for a different underlying reason (401 auth failure instead of 404 not-found). Verified the backend endpoint itself is correct: the same GET with a valid WP Application Password returns 200 with the real balance. The nonce this code needs already exists on the same page render — `direct_rest_nonce` (wp_create_nonce('wp_rest')) is in blocks/user-dashboard/render.php:1250 and is already rendered as the `data-rest-nonce` attribute on the checkout button — but refreshCreditsBalanceAfterCheckout() never reads it. Net customer impact is unchanged from the original bug card: the live balance confirmation never resolves in-page; only a manual refresh shows the true new balance.
failures.expected: tryFetch() (and claimOnce()) authenticate successfully against the balance/claim endpoints and the banner's balance line updates in-page once the claim/webhook lands, without requiring a manual refresh.
failures.actual: Both fetch calls send an empty X-WP-Nonce header sourced from a global that is never defined, so WordPress logs the request out server-side and check_balance_permission() returns 401 every time. The balance line always degrades to the 30-second timeout message.

A.title: Post-checkout balance poll (view.js balance endpoint URL)
A.summary: The specific bug named in the dispatch (bare-namespace 404) IS fixed — confirmed the network request now correctly targets .../wbcom-credits/v1/wb-listora/balance in both source and the rebuilt bundle. But live browser reproduction found the poll still never resolves: every request returns 401 rest_forbidden because the fetch call (and the neighboring claimOnce() call) send no valid X-WP-Nonce — they read window.listoraDashboard.restNonce, a global that is never localized anywhere in the plugin. The member-visible symptom is unchanged: the banner still falls through to the 30-second timeout copy instead of confirming the new balance in-page. See failures[0] for full root-cause detail and the one-line-scale fix (read the existing data-rest-nonce attribute already rendered on the page, or localize the nonce properly).

D.title: Needs currency validation
D.summary: POST /listora/v1/needs as an authenticated member with currency:"HELLO" returns 400 rest_invalid_param / rest_not_in_enum, listing all 10 valid codes in the error message, and creates nothing. The same request with currency:"EUR" returns 201 and creates the need. Test need deleted after verification. Confirmed by reading includes/rest/class-needs-controller.php: the `currency` REST arg now carries an `enum` from allowed_currencies(), which is built from wb_listora_get_currencies() plus a back-compat allowance for whatever the site's current currency already is.
